text.p: Tourism in Malta fell by 5.6 percent last year to reach 1,053,788 tourist arrivals from 1,115,971 in 1995, the Central Office of Statistics said on Thursday.
The decline in arrivals was steepest on the British market, the island's biggest, which shed 62,260 tourists, or 13.5 per cent, to 398,899.

Smaller drops were recorded in arrivals from France and Italy which were partially made up for by increases in arrivals from Libya (+13,764), the Netherlands (+3,085) and a number of other countries (+4,781).
The decline in arrivals was steepest between March and June and almost levelled out by December when a 0.3 per cent drop was recorded.

Maltese tourism officials have blamed the decline on an increased preference for long-haul destinations, particularly Florida, pointing out that most Mediterranean destinations have seen tourism decline.
But new Tourism Minister Karmenu Vella said in Parliament last week that the government wanted the Maltese tourism product to be more competitive in price and quality.
